history.llm_response:
The type of Lymphoma, specifically B-cell lymphoma, can be classified based on the minimal residual disease (MRD) markers as follows:

1. Pre-T cell lymphoma (cCD3+, CD7+, CD2+, TdT+, CD1a-, CD4-, CD8-, CD34+/-)
2. Cortical T-cell ALL (cCD3+, CD7+, CD1a+, CD2+, CD4+, CD8+, CD34-)
3. Medullary T-cell ALL (sCD3+, cCD3+, CD7+, CD1a-, CD2+, CD4+ or CD8+, CD34-)

These types of lymphoma are classified based on MRD markers, which can help in determining the prognosis and treatment approach. The classification is also related to the risk group:

1. Low-risk group: patients aged 1-10 years, with an initial white blood cell count (WBC) of less than 50,000/mm³, without any abnormal MRD or poor prognosis features such as a low number of leukemia cells (≤44 leukemia cells), the t(9;22), t(4;11), or t(1;19) translocations.
2. High-risk group: patients under 1 year old or over 10 years, or those with an initial WBC of 50,000/mm³ or more, or with any abnormal MRD or poor prognosis features.

Some specific genetic mutations like ABL1 and MLL-AF4 (which belong to the kinase gene family) are associated with high-risk B-cell ALL due to their impact on lymphocyte B cell growth, differentiation, and response to chemotherapy treatment, thus being classified in the high-risk group.

Regarding MRD markers, research has shown that most abnormalities belong to the B-cell lymphoma group (B-ALL), with translocations such as t(9;22) being the most common (6 cases of leukemia).
